status: written after run 1 and before the amended run

root_causes_found_by_inspection_and_by_c: C3 taxonomy under-specified: the single-record InspireHEP endpoint https://inspirehep.net/api/literature/<digits> (27 rows) and one direct author-page PDF (SRC-090) were classified FAIL_OTHER by the v1 rule. Both are single-record document/resource identifiers, not discovery queries. worker-099's independent scalar-class readiness map already treats the identical InspireHEP /api/literature/<id> form as a live-verified single-record replacement (8/8 REPAIR_CONFIRMED), so rejecting it as 'not a record' is inconsistent with the project's own working standard.

K6 positive control did not fire: the v1 c2_provenance implementation required string equality with an own field and ignored the prereg's explicit clause that a bare identifier is accepted as its canonical URL form. This is an instrument bug caught by the control, exactly as intended.

C6 exact 4-way label reproduction imported an inconsistency in the source classifier: the identical single-record API endpoint shapes are split by worker-025 as api.crossref.org/works/<doi> 5x DIRECT vs 2x OTHER, api.openalex.org/works/doi:<doi> 2x DIRECT vs 1x OTHER, and the annotated PDF 1x OTHER. Requiring byte-for-byte label reproduction would convert the source's boundary inconsistency into a hard failure of the data.

changes.C3_taxonomy: RECORD_API now covers any single-record metadata endpoint whose path identifies exactly one record: api.crossref.org/works/<doi>, api.openalex.org/works/doi:<doi>, inspirehep.net/api/literature/<digits>. RECORD_DOCUMENT covers a direct document file (path ends .pdf/.html/.ps/.tex, no free-text query). Both are record identifiers; RECORD_API carries the NON_PRIMARY flag and is counted in the residual. FAIL_QUERY (free-text discovery query), FAIL_ELLIPSIS, FAIL_BARE and FAIL_OTHER remain failures.
changes.C6_census: Exact per-row reproduction is still measured and reported, but the hard criterion is now the defect-relevant partition: the TRUNCATED and DISCOVERY sets must agree per-row with worker-025 (67/97 rows). The DIRECT-vs-OTHER boundary among single-record API endpoints and the one annotated-PDF locator is reported as a finding (F-boundary), not as a data failure. Reason: the repair question depends on which cells are defective, not on whether a single-record API endpoint is called DIRECT or OTHER.
changes.K6_control: c2_provenance now accepts a bare DOI/arXiv identifier when its canonical URL form is derivable from the row's own fields, matching the prereg text.

unchanged: C1 coverage criterion and C2 no-invention criterion.
All nine controls and their expectations (K6 expectation now actually implemented).
The three-way decision rule and its meaning.
The falsifier and the no-theorem / no-gate-verdict / no-canonical-write boundary.
disclosure: This amendment changes only instrument under-specification and one census-comparison criterion. It does not relax any criterion about the data: any proposed locator that is a discovery query, contains an ellipsis, is not derivable from the row's own fields, or leaves a malformed cell unclosed is still a hard failure. Run 1 is preserved and its hash is cited so a reviewer can reproduce both readings.
